question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: Writing clinical drug trials for pharmaceutical companies
options.B: Identifying health problems and community resources
options.C: Assessing hospital staff performance and salaries
options.D: Treating individual patients in a hospital ward

explanation: Community diagnosis focuses on evaluating overall population health needs and available assets to plan effective interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is epidemiology considered essential for community health nursing?

options.A: It prescribes surgical procedures for complicated illnesses
options.B: It determines individual nurse promotions in primary health centres
options.C: It tracks disease distribution and population health patterns
options.D: It manages hospital financial budgets and equipment purchases

explanation: Epidemiology provides the scientific data needed to understand who gets sick and why within a specific population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h1)

question: High population density in households directly influences the spread of which type of disease?
explanation: Crowded living conditions facilitate the rapid transmission of pathogens spread through respiratory droplets or close physical contact. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h2)

question: A community with a high proportion of under-five children requires a primary health care focus on which service?

options.A: Occupational hazard screening for factory workers
options.B: Geriatric palliative care and arthritis management
options.D: Cataract surgery and age-related vision testing

explanation: Young children represent a vulnerable demographic that relies heavily on preventive child health services to reduce infant mortality. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h2)

question: What does morbidity data specifically measure within a community?

options.C: Total number of deaths recorded annually
options.D: Availability of clean drinking water sources

explanation: Morbidity refers strictly to the state of being unhealthy or diseased within a specific population group. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why can relying only on hospital registers give a false impression of community health?

options.A: Many sick people do not visit formal health facilities
options.B: Hospitals only record deaths and ignore all illnesses
options.C: Government records intentionally hide all infectious outbreaks
options.D: Health workers always exaggerate the number of disease cases

explanation: Hospital data only captures those who successfully access care, missing community members who use traditional remedies or stay home. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h3)

question: Open defecation and poor water sources are most directly linked to the spread of which disease?
explanation: Waterborne diseases like cholera spread rapidly when fecal matter contaminates drinking water sources due to poor sanitation. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h4)

question: Poor surface water drainage in a residential area primarily contributes to an increase in what health problem?
explanation: Stagnant water pools resulting from poor drainage serve as ideal breeding grounds for malaria-carrying mosquitoes. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h4)

question: What term describes the conditions in which people live and work that affect their health?
explanation: Socio-economic factors, environment, and education form the broader social determinants that heavily dictate population well-being. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h5)

question: A patient with low household income and poor education is most likely to experience what barrier to healthcare?

options.A: Immediate access to specialized private surgical specialists
options.B: Delayed health-seeking due to financial and transport constraints
options.C: Over-compliance with complex multi-drug prescription regimens
options.D: Excessive reliance on international digital health portals

explanation: Poverty and lack of resources frequently prevent individuals from affording transport and treatment fees until illnesses become severe. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h5)

question: What indicates a failure or lack of trust in local primary health care facilities?

options.A: Village health committees organizing monthly sanitation clean-up days
options.B: Traditional birth attendants referring complicated deliveries to midwives
options.C: Community members utilizing routine immunization services regularly
options.D: Patients bypassing local centres for minor ailments to visit tertiary hospitals

explanation: When basic health posts are underutilized for minor conditions, it usually points to poor service quality, stockouts, or community distrust. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is evaluating the cold chain system critical during a community health assessment?

options.A: It ensures vaccines remain potent and effective during storage and transport
options.B: It monitors the refrigeration capacity for surgical blood transfusion units
options.C: It tracks the distribution speed of oral rehydration salt sachets
options.D: It measures the average daily temperature inside residential kitchens

explanation: Vaccines are temperature-sensitive biological products that lose their potency if the cold chain is broken before administration. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which data collection method uses guided conversations to uncover community attitudes and cultural beliefs?
explanation: Focus groups allow researchers to explore shared community perspectives, beliefs, and attitudes through open-ended dialogue. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why would a community health nurse use direct observation alongside household surveys?

options.A: To diagnose individual chronic illnesses without laboratory equipment
options.B: To replace the need for community meetings and interviews entirely
options.C: To verify if reported living conditions match actual physical realities
options.D: To force residents to clean their compounds before inspection

explanation: Direct observation helps validate survey responses by letting nurses witness environmental and sanitary conditions firsthand. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h7)

question: What factor is most important when deciding which community health problem to tackle first?

options.A: Magnitude and severity of the health problem
options.B: Personal preference of the visiting medical officer
options.C: Complexity of medical terminology used in textbooks
options.D: Availability of foreign travel grants for nurses

explanation: Prioritization depends heavily on how many people are affected and how severely their health and survival are threatened. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why is community participation essential during the health problem prioritization process?

options.A: It prevents nurses from making any independent professional decisions
options.B: It ensures local ownership and commitment to the resulting action plan
options.C: It transfers all financial costs of healthcare to villagers
options.D: It eliminates the need for any epidemiological data collection

explanation: Involving community members builds trust and guarantees that the chosen interventions align with what the community values most. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h8)
